classification.difficultyReason: Identify that the total represents 250% of the wrong answers before applying the unitary method.

content.prompt: On a test containing 30 true/false questions, David gave $50\%$ more right answers than wrong ones. How many questions did he answer correctly?

answer.short:
$18$ questions.

The right answers represent $150\%$ of the wrong answers, so all $30$ answers represent $250\%$ of the wrong answers.
answer.worked:
Taking the number of wrong answers as $100\%$, the number of right answers is $150\%$. Thus all $30$ answers represent $250\%$ of the number of wrong answers.

$$\begin{align*}1\%\text{ of the wrong answers}&=\frac{30}{250}\\150\%\text{ of the wrong answers}&=\frac{30}{250}\times150\\150\%\text{ of the wrong answers}&=18\end{align*}$$

David answered $18$ questions correctly. Check: there were $30-18=12$ wrong answers, and $18-12=6=50\%\times12$.
